keyVerseText: To morrow go ye down against them: behold, they come up by the cliff of Ziz; and ye shall find them at the end of the brook, before the wilderness of Jeruel. cliff: Heb. ascent brook: or, valley
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun סוֹף (çôwph) derives from the root סוּף (çûwph), which conveys the idea of coming to an end, ceasing, or being consumed. This root emphasizes the act of termination or completion, not merely a point in time but the process of concluding or snatching away. Thus, the literal sense of סוֹף extends beyond the English 'end' to include the notion of an ultimate cessation or finality that brings something to its full conclusion.
usageInScripture: Across its five occurrences, סוֹף consistently denotes the concept of an end or conclusion, whether spatially, temporally, or conceptually. Translations such as 'them at the end,' 'to the end,' 'that is the end,' and 'the conclusion' reveal a semantic range centered on finality or completion. The phrase 'and his hinder part' suggests a physical or positional dimension as well. This range underscores סוֹף as a term marking the boundary or termination point of an event, place, or period, reflecting both literal and figurative endings in Scripture.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding סוֹף's original meaning enriches our grasp of biblical themes related to God's sovereign control over beginnings and endings. The term's root sense of termination aligns with the biblical teaching that all things have a divinely appointed conclusion, including human life and God's redemptive work. This highlights the trustworthiness of God's promises, as He ordains the 'end' in accordance with His perfect plan. For the Christian faith, סוֹף reminds believers that God's purposes will reach their full consummation in Christ, assuring us that what He begins, He will faithfully bring to completion.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Chronicles 20:16, the phrase 'ye shall find them at the end of the brook' situates the enemy's position precisely at the סוֹף, or termination point, of a geographical feature. This usage emphasizes the boundary or limit where the confrontation will occur. The word סוֹף here contributes a sense of finality and decisive encounter, reinforcing that God's deliverance will come at the appointed 'end' or boundary, where His people meet and overcome their foes.
